title: Scalar and annihilator compatibility of the bundle zero-section integration adjunct
statement: Let A,B be finite commutative rings, φ:A→B unital, and N,M>0 with M dividing N, NA=0 and MB=0. Let S be Noetherian with N and M invertible, let d≥0, and let E be a locally free O_S-module of constant rank d, with actual vector bundle π and zero section z [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section]. Let t be the root-power, root-generator and derived-counit normalized coefficient-line comparison [def-pur-finite-smooth-coefficient-arrows]. Let a_A and a_B denote the actual Kummer-normalized bundle integration adjuncts restricted to z, at annihilators N and M respectively [lem-trf-finite-ring-section-deformation]. Let q_(π,z) be the actual exceptional coefficient section map [def-pur-dnc-coefficient-section-maps], using the canonical vector-bundle compactification. Then Q_S(a_A) ≫ q_(π,z) = (t.tensorPower d).hom ≫ a_B. No deformation family, ambient smooth section, cone-to-bundle map or choice of smooth orientation occurs.

proof.text: Use the trace equation finiteVectorIntegration_scalar, which factors the coefficient comparison through the common exponent N and uses the existing vector scalar-descent and general-ring integration exponent theorems.

The compact-support coefficient natural transformation is componentwise invertible by etaleCompactScalarCoherence. Assemble its component inverses into the isomorphism q. Apply adjunction naturality and the triangle identity (private scalar_adjunct) to the trace equation. The inverse component is exactly ExceptionalCoefficients.comparisonInverse. Unfolding the specified mate yields the scalar equation for the actual bundle integration adjunct.

Apply the zero-section pullback functor. Naturality moves the bundle adjunct past the scalar/pullback comparison. The scalar_section_compositor identity identifies the remaining section-compositor factors. The private section_square proves this categorical calculation explicitly and gives the two bundleSectionAdjoint maps. The statement and coefficient tensor order are unchanged.
